hypotheses.reasoning: The origin is the external identity provider (idp.example/oauth2/token) called by auth-svc. Starting at 05:39:12 (#182) its calls slow from 4.5s to 11-13s (#183, #185), well above the 2s soft threshold. By 05:40:43 (#190) they hang until the 30s timeout. Each hung IdP call holds an auth-svc request, so account-svc's calls to auth-svc /tokens time out (#191, #205). account-svc's connection pool to auth-svc then saturates at 50/50 with a growing queue (#215, #219, #224, #232), pool checkout timeouts follow (#243), and edge-proxy returns 503s on POST /login with 5-26s latency (#211 onward). The 5xx at edge-proxy and the pool saturation are downstream symptoms and are not cited. The rate-limit 429 on client k-7858 (#181) and the audit-consumer GC pause (#164) are unrelated to the failure path. accounts-db and session-cache show no errors. The IdP returned slowness and timeouts, not error codes, which fits dependency_timeout rather than external_outage. The logs do not show the IdP's own status, so the hung-IdP reading rests on the timeout pattern.

If the identity provider is reporting itself down, this would be an external outage. The logs show slowness and timeouts with no explicit error codes or status page, so this reading is less likely than a hang.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the identity provider owners and check idp.example status and latency. In the meantime, lower the auth-svc IdP call timeout well below 30s and add a circuit breaker so hung calls fail fast. Also raise or size the account-svc to auth-svc connection pool limit, or shed load, so queued requests stop piling up. Once IdP latency recovers, verify that /login 503s clear.
